text:
maria: Quick sync — product asked us to produce a PRD + acceptance matrix for the planned runtime changes: kernel selection policy, attention optimizations, and KV cache retention. AtlasPay has three must-haves: deterministic p95, opt-in accuracy-first kernel, and KV isolation for private deployments. Need clear launch criteria by EOD Fri.

devon: Ack. Do we treat attention opt as a single feature toggle or per-model? leaning per-model.

alex: Short list of acceptance criteria I propose:
- Functional: kernel selection must choose a compatible kernel automatically for (model, seq_len) within 10ms decision latency.
- Perf: p95 token latency end-to-end <= 120ms on our standard 8k sequence harness (8xA100 equivalent).
- QoS: output divergence <= 1% on our eval prompt set.
- Safety: fallback to stable kernel if quality regression > 1.5% OR p99 latency > 300ms during ramp.
(put that in the PRD). :+1:

sam: +1. Add metrics hooks: per-request kernel_id, cache_hit/miss, kv_eviction_reason. I'll draft the measurement queries and attach in doc. link: https://rwd.redwood/docs/rfcs/attn-kv-metrics

arjun: Edgecases to call out: long-running chat sessions where KV grows unbounded — need eviction thresholds by token-count and memory cap, and a `pin` API to keep prefixes in cache. Also define migration semantics when switching kernel variant for an in-progress session (keep KV compatibility).

sarah: From product: customers care about predictable billing. Add acceptance for cost delta: <= 15% per-token for default config. Also require explicit opt-in for quantized/cost-saving kernels.

james: ML note: attention opt B increases throughput but shifts token distribution for long contexts. Add a human/regression test: use a 500-prompt customer sim set + human quality check; require <0.5 point avg delta on our rubric.

deploy-bot: deploybot: New RFC draft published by @maria: https://rwd.redwood/rfcs/runtime-kernel-kv-v1 — status: draft

maria: Proposed PRD scope (v1):
- kernel selection policy: auto + explicit override
- KV cache: default eviction LRU + pin API + per-customer retention cap
- attention toggle: safe-fast variant with automatic fallback
Out of scope: per-request micro-profiling, multi-tenant cache compaction (target v2).

maria: Next steps / owners:
- dev (devon/sam): create RFC skeleton with acceptance bullets — due Tue COB
- perf (alex/sam): perf harness + measurement queries — due Wed
- product/security (sarah): billing wording + KMS implications — due Thu
- ML (james): regression harness + human eval plan — due Thu

devon: I will spin up the RFC skeleton. Quick Q: do we need canary gating by region or by customer? recommend customer pilot (AtlasPay) + region canary in us-east-1.

maria: Agree: pilot via customer flag + canary in us-east-1 for 10% traffic. Rollback automatically if p99 or quality thresholds breach within 15m.

alex: Can we standardize a one-line acceptance template to paste into the PRD? e.g.:

```
ACCEPTANCE: [metric] <= [value] measured on [harness] over [window] with [traffic profile]
```

maria: Perfect — I'll paste that as the canonical format.

sarah: Please add a launch checklist with mandatory sign-offs: security review, billing docs, customer comms, migration runbook, and QA sign-off.

maria: Will do. I'll post the RFC skeleton link here when ready. Tagging @devon @sam @alex for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

devon: Thanks — starting skeleton now.

sam: I'll drop initial measurement SQL and example Grafana queries into the RFC once skeleton exists.

maria: Closing loop — thanks everyone. If you have small TODOs please add them as comments in the RFC rather than here.
